# Implementation Plan: Tier-1 Hermetic E2E Conversation-Simulation Harness for `remote_session`
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"codex-autoconnect-e2e-conversation-simulation-harness"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-22. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/codex-autoconnect-e2e-conversation-simulation-harness/plan.md`.*

## Overview

The shipped raw-codex Happy autoconnect feature (`remote_session`, the `codex-happy` overlay
crate) has every *piece* unit-tested in isolation — crypto KATs, REST `/v3` send/backfill against
a `wiremock` mock, inbound-control mapping as pure functions, outbound transcript mapping as pure
functions — but **no retained automated test wires inbound → turn → outbound as a loop, and none
drives the tool-approval round-trip.** The operator's question *"did we test the happy support for
our codex — conversation and all?"* therefore has no green CI answer today.

This plan builds **Tier 1** of the brainstorm's two-tier design (D-001): a hermetic, deterministic,
always-on `cargo test -p codex-happy` integration harness that drives `attach.rs`'s full routing
loop with **injected channel seams** — canned `AppServerEvent`s on the outbound tap, injected
`InboundEvent`s on the inbound channel, and a **fake `AppServerRequestHandle`** — asserting a full
simulated conversation (text-turn round-trip + tool-approval approve/deny round-trip + abort +
AEAD-drop + default-off), with **no real model, socket, tunnel, auth, or elevation**, so it rides
`.github/workflows/invariant-check.yml`. A small **overlay-internal** enabling refactor makes the
loop drivable from a test without the real `app.rs` TUI / app-server.

**Tiers 2 and 3 are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE** for this task (operator chose Tier 1 only,
2026-06-22) and are flagged as staged future phases at the end of this plan.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context
*Seeded from brainstorm: `.ralph/brainstorms/codex-autoconnect-e2e-conversation-simulation-harness/selected-direction.md` (D-001).*

All target source is in the codex submodule overlay crate
`codex/codex-rs-overlay/codex-happy/` (fork-exclusive; zero upstream-conflict surface per
`codex/CLAUDE.md` tenet #1). Key seams (verified first-hand + by two research agents):

- **`attach.rs::run_attach(params, request_handle: AppServerRequestHandle, rx: UnboundedReceiver<AppServerEvent>)`** (private, 141-145) is the heart. It runs `establish()` (creds → Happy session → real `rust_socketio` connect; 251-286) concurrently with a pre-connect drain, then a steady-state `tokio::select!` loop (begins ~193) draining `rx` (outbound codex events → `map_event` → encrypt → POST `/v3`) + `inbound_rx` (mobile `InboundEvent`s → drive `request_handle`) + a 2 s keepalive (guarded by `client.is_connected()`).
- The only `request_handle` methods the loop uses: `request_typed::<TurnStartResponse>` (393), `request_typed::<TurnSteerResponse>` (374), `resolve_server_request` (421-423, 461-463), `request` (445-446, interrupt). **No `reject_server_request`.**
- **`SessionClient::new(config, initial_state) -> (Self, UnboundedReceiver<InboundEvent>)`** (session.rs:187-205) initializes `socket: None`, `connected: false` — it is **buildable against a `wiremock` `base_url` with no socket connected** (the existing `session_tests.rs` pattern). `send_session_message` (340-380) does serialize → `encrypt` → base64 → POST `/v3/sessions/:id/messages`; `is_connected()` is false until `connect()`, so the keepalive arm never fires under test.
- **`ControlState`** (inbound.rs:90-169): `observe(&event)` sets `primary_thread_id` from a root `ThreadStarted`/first `TurnStarted` and tracks `active_turn_id`; `plan_turn(text) -> Option<TurnAction::{Start,Steer}>`; `plan_interrupt() -> Option<ClientRequest>`. A mobile `UserMessage` only drives a `TurnStart` once `primary_thread_id` is set (otherwise it is buffered in `pending_user_messages`).
- **`map_event`** (mapping.rs:52-67): `TurnStarted → SessionEvent::TurnStart {}`; `ItemCompleted(AgentMessage{text}) → SessionEvent::Text { text, thinking: None }`; `TurnCompleted → SessionEvent::TurnEnd { status }`. So a canned codex turn decrypts on the wire to `TurnStart {}` → `Text { … }` → `TurnEnd { … }`.
- **`encryption::{encrypt,decrypt}(key:&[u8;32], variant: EncryptionVariant, data)`** (244-258) — the test decrypts captured `/v3` POST bodies.
- **Reusable fixtures** already exist: `turn_started`/`turn_completed`/`item_started`/`exec_v2`/`file_change_v2` (inbound_tests.rs), `agent_message`/`item_completed`/`command_execution` (mapping_tests.rs), `config`/`initial_state`/`encrypt_body`/`stored_message` (session_tests.rs). Test modules are wired `#[cfg(test)] #[path = "<x>_tests.rs"] mod tests;`.
- **Dev-deps already present** in `codex-happy/Cargo.toml`: `wiremock`, `tokio {macros, rt-multi-thread}`, `tempfile`, `codex-utils-absolute-path`. **No new dependency is required.**

### Technical Constraints
- **The fake handle cannot be built directly.** `app-server-client/src/lib.rs`: `InProcessAppServerRequestHandle { command_tx: mpsc::Sender<ClientCommand> }` has a **private** `command_tx` (458-461) and **no public constructor** reachable from an external crate. Constructing `AppServerRequestHandle::InProcess(..)` from `codex-happy` would require an **upstream-canonical edit** — which the operator-accepted constraint forbids ("confirm overlay-internal, NO upstream codex edits"). **Resolution (confirmed feasible):** define a **local trait** in `codex-happy` and implement it for the *foreign* `AppServerRequestHandle` (the orphan rule permits a local trait + foreign type). `run_attach_core` becomes generic over that trait; the real `run_attach` passes the real handle; the test passes a fake. **Zero upstream edits.** → The brainstorm's disconfirming observation ("if the fake handle can't be built without widening upstream APIs, Tier 1 loses its zero-conflict advantage") is **resolved** — the trait seam avoids the upstream widening.
- `happy_tap` only fires inside the real `tui/src/app.rs` TUI loop; a `cargo test` cannot run the literal tee. Tier 1 therefore drives `run_attach_core` **directly** at the channel seam, not via `app.rs`. ✔ consistent with the constraint.
- `rust_socketio` is client-side and `wiremock` cannot speak Socket.IO; Tier 1 injects at the channel seam (own `inbound_rx`), not a faked socket. ✔
- The model turn cannot be a real Copilot/Claude call (ETW/elevation + the copilot provider's fail-closed `base_url`); the codex turn is always canned `AppServerEvent`s. ✔
- The async future returned by `request_typed::<T>` (and the other trait methods) **must be `Send`**, because `run_attach`/`run_attach_core` is `tokio::spawn`ed (attach.rs:120). Concretely the trait needs a `Send + Sync` supertrait, futures spelled `+ Send + '_`, the generic method bounded `T: DeserializeOwned + Send + 'static`, and `run_attach_core<H: AppServerHandle + 'static>` (see the exact signature in Architecture below). The real handle's methods only await `Send` channel ops and hold no `!Send` state across awaits, so this is satisfiable; it is a story-level verification point for US-001.

## Approach

### Architecture
A two-part change, both **entirely inside `codex-rs-overlay/codex-happy/`** (zero upstream-canonical
edits ⇒ no new `// SANDBOX PATCH:` markers, no new `patch-surface.md` §14/§15 rows):

1. **Enabling refactor (behavior-preserving):**
   - Extract a `run_attach_core(...)` from `run_attach` at the post-establish boundary (after `attach.rs:188`; loop begins ~190/193). `run_attach` keeps `establish()` + the pre-connect drain, then calls `run_attach_core(client, inbound_rx, request_handle, rx, control, buffer, pending_approvals, pending_user_messages)`.
   - Define a `pub(crate) trait AppServerHandle` exposing exactly the methods the loop calls — `request`, `request_typed::<T>`, and `resolve_server_request` — as native RPITIT methods with explicit `Send` bounds (per the codex-patched AGENTS.md "no `#[async_trait]`" rule). Implement it once for `codex_app_server_client::AppServerRequestHandle` (a thin delegating impl). The seam is roughly:
     ```rust
     pub(crate) trait AppServerHandle: Send + Sync {
         fn request(&self, request: ClientRequest) -> impl Future<Output = IoResult<RequestResult>> + Send + '_;
         fn request_typed<T>(&self, request: ClientRequest) -> impl Future<Output = Result<T, TypedRequestError>> + Send + '_
         where T: DeserializeOwned + Send + 'static;
         fn resolve_server_request(&self, request_id: RequestId, result: JsonRpcResult) -> impl Future<Output = IoResult<()>> + Send + '_;
     }
     ```
   - Make `run_attach_core` and the eight helpers that take `&AppServerRequestHandle` (`handle_inbound`, `enqueue_or_drive_turn`, `flush_pending_turns`, `drive_turn`, `start_turn`, `handle_permission`, `handle_abort`, `cancel_pending_approvals`) generic over `H: AppServerHandle`; the spawned `run_attach_core<H: AppServerHandle + 'static>`. Mechanical signature plumbing.
   - *Optional simplification the implementer may choose:* if the generic `request_typed<T>` fake proves awkward, expose semantic concrete-return methods on the trait (`start_turn -> TurnStartResponse`, `steer_turn -> TurnSteerResponse`, `interrupt`, `resolve`) instead of raw `request_typed<T>`. Either shape is zero-upstream-edit; pick whichever keeps the fake cleanest.

2. **The Tier-1 harness** in a new in-crate sibling `attach_e2e_tests.rs`, wired `#[cfg(test)] #[path = "attach_e2e_tests.rs"] mod e2e_tests;` (reaches `pub(crate)` items, **zero public-API growth**, matches the existing convention and the codex-patched "keep crate API surface small" rule — preferred over the brainstorm's `tests/` dir which would force a `pub` surface):
   - `FakeAppServerHandle` implementing `AppServerHandle`: records the `ClientRequest`s it receives and the `resolve_server_request(request_id, payload)` calls (behind a shared `Arc<Mutex<…>>` so the test can assert after driving), and returns canned `TurnStartResponse` (`{ turn: Turn{ id } }`) / `TurnSteerResponse` (`{ turnId }`) — built as a `serde_json::Value` matching the incoming `ClientRequest` variant and `from_value::<T>`'d (verified viable for both response types).
   - **Fixtures must be DUPLICATED locally, not reused.** The existing fixture builders (`config`/`initial_state`/`encrypt_body` in session_tests.rs, `turn_started`/`exec_v2`/`file_change_v2` in inbound_tests.rs, `agent_message`/`item_completed` in mapping_tests.rs) are **private fns in sibling `#[cfg(test)]` modules** — a child module of `attach.rs` cannot call them. Copy the minimal needed fixtures into `attach_e2e_tests.rs` (keeps the "only attach.rs + the new file" scope; a shared `pub(crate)` test_support module is an option but widens the file footprint and is not recommended).
   - A wiremock-backed outbound sink: build a real `SessionClient` against a `wiremock` `MockServer` whose `POST /v3/sessions/:id/messages` handler captures request bodies; a decrypt helper (`encryption::decrypt` + base64) reconstructs the transcript `SessionEnvelope`s. **Gotcha (verified, session.rs:367-371):** `send_session_message` parses the POST response and looks up the delivery by the request's `localId`; the wiremock responder must be a dynamic `wiremock::Respond` impl that echoes the request's `localId` back with a `seq` (e.g. `{"messages":[{"id":"m1","seq":N,"localId":"<echoed>"}]}`), or `send_envelope` logs a swallowed error. (`send_session_message` is purely HTTP — no socket/`connect()`/CAS dependency — so no live socket is needed.)
   - **Two inbound wiring modes.** For RPC/turn scenarios (text-turn, approval, abort) the test owns a fresh `inbound_tx`/`inbound_rx` and injects `InboundEvent`s directly. For the **AEAD-drop** scenario the test must instead pass `run_attach_core` the `inbound_rx` **returned by `SessionClient::new`** and drive `client.fetch_messages()` against a wiremock GET that returns an *undecryptable* encrypted message — so the real `decrypt_and_route` early-drop (session.rs:629-633) is exercised; direct `InboundEvent` injection would bypass the crypto boundary and prove nothing.
   - A small driver: spawn `run_attach_core` on a `tokio::task`, hold the tap `tx` (and the relevant `inbound_tx`), inject events, drive to a **deterministic barrier** (see Risk Areas) rather than a bare `yield_now`, then drop the tap `tx` to break the loop and `await` the task before asserting against the shared `Arc<Mutex>`.

### Implementation Strategy
Ordered, serial (every story touches `attach.rs` and/or the single new test file → must land in
sequence):
1. **US-001** — the enabling refactor (trait + `run_attach_core` + genericize) **plus adding the `#[cfg(test)] #[path = "attach_e2e_tests.rs"] mod e2e_tests;` wiring to `attach.rs`** (with a minimal placeholder test in the new file so it compiles). Behavior-preserving; gated by the *existing* `attach_tests.rs` + `cargo check`.
2. **US-002** — harness scaffolding (`FakeAppServerHandle`, wiremock sink helper, driver) + the **text-turn round-trip** scenario (the cheapest validation that the whole loop wires).
3. **US-003** — the **tool-approval round-trip**: approve, deny, first-resolve-wins dedup, and a malformed-decision case pinning the **current** resolve-payload behavior.
4. **US-004** — **abort/interrupt**, **AEAD-failure drop**, **default-off**.

### Files to Create/Modify
- **Modify** `codex/codex-rs-overlay/codex-happy/src/attach.rs` — extract `run_attach_core`; add `AppServerHandle` trait + orphan impl; genericize 8 helpers; add the `#[cfg(test)] #[path] mod e2e_tests;` wiring.
- **Create** `codex/codex-rs-overlay/codex-happy/src/attach_e2e_tests.rs` — the Tier-1 harness (fake handle, wiremock sink helper, locally-duplicated minimal fixtures, 5 scenarios).
- **No other files.** Specifically **do not** touch anything under `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/` (esp. `app-server-client/src/lib.rs`, `tui/src/app.rs`).

## Scope

### In Scope
- The overlay-internal enabling refactor (`run_attach_core` + `AppServerHandle` trait + genericized helpers), behavior-preserving.
- The hermetic Tier-1 harness asserting, as a wired loop: text-turn round-trip; approval approve **and** deny + first-resolve-wins dedup + malformed→deny; abort/interrupt; AEAD-failure drop; default-off.
- Minimal **locally-duplicated** fixtures (sibling test-module fns are private) + the **existing** `wiremock` dev-dep — **no new dependency**; the harness is retained (committed), CI-safe, and rides `invariant-check.yml`.

### Out of Scope
- **Tier 2 (staged future task):** an opt-in `#[ignore]`/env-gated `live_*` test against the **real** `packages/happy-server` (tunnel-mode-127.0.0.1, deterministic PGlite) with a Rust "mobile" client over the **real socket + real crypto-on-wire** — promoting the deleted US-001 probe (carry the `/v1/updates/` trailing-slash + `dataEncryptionKey:null` gotchas).
- **Tier 3 / D-002 (spike-gated future task):** a real in-process codex app-server driven by a stubbed model through the literal `app.rs` tee.
- Any real authenticated model turn; any change to `packages/happy-server`; any edit under `external/repos/codex-patched/`.

## Risk Areas
- **`tokio::select!` non-determinism + ordering barrier.** The loop selects independently between the outbound tap and inbound channel (attach.rs:193-239), so events injected back-to-back can be processed out of order. Approval state is only inserted when the **outbound** `ServerRequest` branch runs (attach.rs:195-202), while `handle_permission` drops unknown ids (attach.rs:416-419) — so sending an approval `ServerRequest` and a `permission` RPC back-to-back can flakily process the permission first and no-op. **Mitigation:** after injecting the approval, wait for a *deterministic observable* that proves the outbound queue advanced past it (e.g. inject a mapped transcript event after the approval and `await` until its `/v3` POST is captured — FIFO on the single tap then proves the approval was processed) before injecting the `permission`. Do **not** rely on `yield_now` as a correctness barrier. End each scenario by dropping the tap `tx` and `await`ing the spawned task before asserting.
- **No `start_paused` without a new dev-dep.** `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` requires Tokio's `test-util` feature, which is **not** in `codex-happy`'s dev-deps (only `macros` + `rt-multi-thread`). Stay zero-new-dependency: drive determinism via the observable barriers above, not a paused clock. (The keepalive arm never fires anyway — `is_connected()` is false without `connect()`.)
- **`primary_thread_id` priming yields Start vs Steer (verified, important).** `observe(TurnStarted)` adopts the thread **and sets `active_turn_id`** (inbound.rs:121-125); `plan_turn` then returns **`TurnSteer`** whenever `active_turn_id` is `Some` (inbound.rs:194-218). So to make a mobile `UserMessage` drive a **`TurnStart`**, prime the primary thread *without* an active turn: inject a root **`ThreadStarted`** (`parent_thread_id == None` → `lock_primary_if_root` sets only `primary_thread_id`, inbound.rs:118-120/183-187), or an `ItemStarted` (adopts thread without active), or `TurnStarted`+`TurnCompleted` (clears active). Use `ThreadStarted` for the canonical "primary thread up, idle" state. A `UserMessage` injected before any primary-thread event is *buffered* (attach.rs:333-346); a separate assertion can cover the buffered-then-flushed path.
- **`Send` bound on the trait futures** (spawned future). Verify `cargo check -p codex-happy` after US-001 with the exact bounds in Architecture (`Send + Sync` supertrait, `+ Send + '_`, `T: DeserializeOwned + Send + 'static`, `run_attach_core<H: ... + 'static>`).
- **Scenario overlap with existing tests** — call it out, don't duplicate: default-off feature gate is structurally enforced by invariant 55 (`happy_seam_invariants.rs:148-167`); undecryptable-message drop has a focused test `backfill_skips_undecryptable_messages` (session_tests.rs). Tier 1's new value is asserting these **through the wired loop** (the AEAD-drop scenario drives the real `decrypt_and_route` via the `SessionClient` inbound path so no action reaches the fake handle; default-off asserts the `should_skip_attach` idempotency path) — not re-proving the unit-level facts.
- **Build environment.** Verification needs the LLVM/xwin frozen iteration env (`source scripts/iteration-env.sh`); `cargo test -p codex-happy` / `cargo check --workspace` run from `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs`. `cargo build --release` is **not** required for this test-only change.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A `cargo test -p codex-happy` integration test drives a **text-turn conversation round-trip** end-to-end through `run_attach_core`: the scenario **first injects a root `ThreadStarted` (`parent_thread_id == None`) so `ControlState::primary_thread_id` is set WITHOUT an active turn** (injecting `TurnStarted` instead would set `active_turn_id` and yield a `TurnSteer`, not a `TurnStart` — inbound.rs:121-125/194-218), then an injected mobile `UserMessage` produces an asserted **`TurnStart`** on the fake handle, and a canned codex turn (`turn_started` → `item_completed(agent_message)` → `turn_completed`) produces encrypted `/v3` envelopes that **decrypt to `TurnStart {}` → `Text { … }` → `TurnEnd { … }`** — with no network, model, socket, or auth. (A complementary assertion may cover the buffered-then-flushed path when the `UserMessage` arrives before any primary-thread event.)
- The same suite asserts the **tool-approval round-trip for BOTH approve and deny** (correct `resolve_server_request` payload on the fake handle), the **first-resolve-wins dedup** (a duplicate mobile decision yields exactly one resolve — `pending_approvals.remove` consumes the entry), and a **malformed-decision** case that asserts the **current** `inbound::resolve_payload` + `canonical_decision` output (not a new semantic): `approved` is authoritative — `approved:true` + unknown decision canonicalizes to `approved`; `approved:false`/missing canonicalizes to `abort` (v2 → `cancel`) unless the decision is exactly `denied`; a missing `id` is a no-op (attach.rs:408-419). The test pins these existing behaviors and proves no panic.
- The suite covers **abort/interrupt**, the **AEAD-failure drop**, and **default-off**, each asserted via overlay-only observable evidence: abort interrupts the active turn (asserted `request`/interrupt `ClientRequest` on the fake handle) and cancels pending approvals (asserted cancel `resolve_server_request`); the AEAD-failure drop is observed by driving the `SessionClient` inbound decrypt path with an undecryptable message and asserting **no `InboundEvent` reaches the loop and no fake-handle action fires** (i.e. the wired loop takes no action — distinct from re-proving the unit-level `backfill_skips_undecryptable_messages`); default-off is asserted at the overlay seam (`should_skip_attach`/`maybe_attach` returns `None` under the `HAPPY_CURRENT_SESSION_ID` idempotency env) with a code cross-reference to invariant 55 for the `app.rs` feature gate (which is out of scope for a `cargo test -p codex-happy`). All deterministic.
- The enabling refactor is **overlay-internal only**: `git diff --name-only` for the change is confined to `codex/codex-rs-overlay/codex-happy/`; **zero files under `external/repos/codex-patched/` are modified**; the pre-existing `attach_tests.rs` still passes; `cargo check --workspace` is green.
- The harness is **retained** (committed), honestly named (Tier 1 = overlay-loop integration test), and a reviewer can read one test and see the full simulated path (mobile message → inbound → turn → outbound → mobile-side decrypt + assert).

## Preliminary Story Decomposition
- **US-001:** Extract `run_attach_core` + add the overlay-internal `AppServerHandle` trait (+ orphan impl), genericize the eight handle-taking helpers, **and add the new `#[cfg(test)] #[path = "attach_e2e_tests.rs"] mod e2e_tests;` module wiring (with a placeholder so the crate compiles).** Behavior-preserving.
- **US-002:** Tier-1 harness scaffolding (`FakeAppServerHandle`, wiremock outbound sink + decrypt helper, driver) + the text-turn round-trip scenario.
- **US-003:** Tool-approval round-trip scenarios — approve, deny, first-resolve-wins dedup, malformed→deny.
- **US-004:** Abort/interrupt, AEAD-failure drop, and default-off scenarios.

## Suggested Decomposition
All stories edit `attach.rs` and/or the single new `attach_e2e_tests.rs`, so they share the same
files and **must run serially** — one cluster, four sequential phases. No parallelism is available
or safe for this task.

### Cluster: tier1-harness
- Stories: [US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004]
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`codex/codex-rs-overlay/codex-happy/src/attach.rs`, `codex/codex-rs-overlay/codex-happy/src/attach_e2e_tests.rs`]; exclusive=[]; risk=high (same two files across all stories)
- `execution_mode` rationale: Serial. Every story mutates `attach.rs` and the single new test file; parallel execution would guarantee merge conflicts and broken intermediate compiles. The stories are also strictly ordered (refactor → scaffolding → scenarios).

Parallel handoff: `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/codex-autoconnect-e2e-conversation-simulation-harness/plan.md --parallel --suggested-decomposition D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/codex-autoconnect-e2e-conversation-simulation-harness/suggested-decomposition.json` *(not recommended here — single serial cluster; prefer the serial handoff.)*

## Open Questions
- **Trait shape (implementer's choice, both zero-upstream-edit):** raw-handle trait (`request`/`request_typed<T>`/`resolve_server_request`) vs semantic-method trait (`start_turn`/`steer_turn`/`interrupt`/`resolve`). The plan recommends the raw-handle trait for the smallest call-site delta, but if the generic `<H>` plumbing or the generic-`T` fake spreads awkwardly across the eight helpers, US-001 may switch to the semantic-method trait (concrete return types, non-generic helpers). Either is zero-upstream-edit.
- **Malformed-decision is a PIN, not a new "deny" semantic.** The plan asserts the *current* `resolve_payload`/`canonical_decision` behavior for missing/garbage decisions (approved-authoritative; false/missing → abort→cancel unless exactly `denied`). If the desired product behavior is actually "invalid ⇒ decline", that is a **behavior change** and must be a separate story — it is explicitly NOT folded into this test-only harness.
- **Default-off assertion granularity (confirmed-but-flagged).** The feature-gate default-off (`Feature::RemoteSession`) lives in `app.rs` (upstream seam) and is already structurally enforced by invariant 55; a `cargo test -p codex-happy` cannot exercise the `app.rs` gate. Tier 1's ownable default-off assertion is therefore the overlay-level idempotency skip (`should_skip_attach`) plus a code cross-reference to invariant 55.
- *(No blocking open questions: the enabling refactor is confirmed overlay-internal with zero upstream edits — both the orphan-rule trait impl and the wiremock outbound sink were verified against source.)*
